subject: Request: US‑West only + no‑fallback for Atlas Health pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot requirement: US‑West only + no fallback for PHI QA workflows

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Atlas' engineering and security teams are aligned and have one strict constraint for the pilot: any inference requests that touch PHI must be served from our designated US‑West region only and must not be allowed to failover to other model variants or regions (no automatic fallback). This is a hard requirement from our compliance and legal teams while the BAA is being finalized.

We're attaching the signed exception form and our SOC2 questionnaire sections that reference residency controls. Can your team confirm whether Redwood can enforce a per‑customer routing policy that: 
- pins requests for a specific model family to us‑west clusters, and
- rejects or returns a clear error (rather than failing over) when the pinned capacity is unavailable?

We understand the operational risk and are prepared to accept increased latency during incidents for the pilot, but we need explicit non‑fallback behavior. Looking for a short yes/no and any required runbook notes we should include.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Senior PM, Integrations
Atlas Health

Attachments: atlas-soc2-questionnaire.pdf, atlas-exception-request-signed.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot requirement: US‑West only + no fallback for PHI QA workflows

Thanks Samantha — looping in SecOps (Irene), Ops (Marcus) and Product (Grace) to confirm feasibility. High level: we do have per‑customer routing and model pinning, but the no‑fallback semantics are atypical for production SLOs. Before we give Atlas a final answer I need: 

1) A short set of acceptance criteria from legal/security (Samantha, thanks for the questionnaire; the signed PDF helps).
2) SecOps risk signoff on rejecting traffic versus fallback (Irene).
3) Ops runbook for capacity loss scenarios if we implement reject‑on‑miss (Marcus).

Marissa / team — can someone draft a minimal implementation plan and list of telemetry/alerting requirements? I'd like a proposed timeline for an ops‑only toggle we can enable for this customer during the pilot window.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot requirement: US‑West only + no fallback for PHI QA workflows

FW: proposed minimal plan below.

On implementation: we can implement a per‑tenant policy that enforces: 
- model_pin: tag 'atlas_pilot_v1' -> route only to us‑west capacity pool
- fallback_behavior: 'reject_with_412' (client receives structured error and retryable flag set to false)

Operational caveats: 
- When us‑west capacity is saturated or partitioned, requests will be rejected. We need Atlas to accept this in writing (their signed exception covers it, but legal should confirm).
- For the pilot we recommend a canary window (2 business days) with doubled headroom reservation so we can test failure modes.
- Must enable extended tracing and per‑request tags for PHI workload so we can exclude it from any cross‑tenant caching.

Telemetry and alerts (minimum): 
- Per‑tenant rejection rate > 0.5% -> page Ops oncall
- Per‑tenant average token latency > 95th pct baseline -> page SRE
- Missing KV cache hits for pinned model -> auto‑create alert for engineering review

Irene/Marcus — can you confirm runbook steps for a rejected state? I'll draft a short YAML we can push for the pilot (attached: usw-no-fallback-proposal.yaml).

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: usw-no-fallback-proposal.yaml
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot requirement: US‑West only + no fallback for PHI QA workflows

Thanks for the summary. Security assessment (high level):

- Residency + non‑fallback: acceptable for a limited pilot if Atlas accepts documented risk (we need a signed exception, which they provided).
- Controls required before enabling: 
  * Per‑tenant keying of routing policy (already supported)
  * Strict audit logging of all rejected requests and full request IDs for later review
  * Encrypted telemetry pipeline with retention aligned to their contract (confirm retention window)

Risk notes:
- Rejecting on capacity loss prevents transparent failover but increases availability risk for the customer. Recommend a mandatory daily health check report for the pilot window and a 24/7 oncall rotation during the first week.

Runbook (short):
1) Confirm headroom reservation in us‑west (Marcus).
2) Enable policy in staging and run synthetic workload for 24h.
3) Enable in pilot with monitoring hooks and legal confirmation of signed exception.
4) If rejection rate > 1% for > 30m, enable emergency rollback and notify Atlas that fallback will be re‑enabled.

I'll sign off once Marcus confirms the headroom/reservation and we've verified the audit logs.

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot requirement: US‑West only + no fallback for PHI QA workflows

Quick ops update: we can reserve a soft pool in us‑west for the pilot (48 GPU‑hr/day) — that should cover their expected volume if they stay within the pilot SLA (per their onboarding doc). Steps completed/planned: 
- Soft reservation configured for tenant: atlas_pilot_v1 (soft limit, auto‑reject on exceed)
- Staging runbook executed this morning; synthetic runs show reject behavior returns a 412 with structured json body as requested.
- Added extra trace fields: tenant_id, request_class, model_pin_id, pilot_flag.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa — push the usw-no-fallback-proposal.yaml to staging and run a 24h soak (you already have the YAML attached).
2) Karthik — can you confirm Atlas legal has accepted the operational risk so we can flip the toggle on Wednesday morning? If yes, I'll schedule the oncall rotation and set the pager thresholds Irene requested.

Marcus
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
